flow_scenarios: Neutral: Main spool centers; P is blocked by the compensator; A and B lines are vented to T; load is held by the dual pilot-operated check valves.

Actuation CLOSE (Port A): Main spool shifts; flow travels P -> compensator -> spool -> Port A line -> PO check valve -> Port A out. Pressure on A line pilots open the Port B check valve, allowing return flow from Port B -> spool -> T rail.

Actuation OPEN (Port B): Main spool shifts; flow travels P -> compensator -> spool -> Port B line -> PO check valve -> Port B out. Pressure on B line pilots open the Port A check valve, allowing return flow from Port A -> spool -> T rail.

Shock/Relief: If external forces cause pressure to spike above 125 bar on A or 195 bar on B while neutral, the respective shock valve opens to vent excess pressure to the T line, while parallel check valves open from T to prevent cavitation.
ports: A (CLOSE, connects off-sheet to transom door actuator)

flow_scenarios: Neutral: Main spool in open center position connects A and B lines to tank; load is held securely by the dual pilot-operated check valves.

Actuation A (CLOSE): Flow travels from P rail through compensator and spool to A port; pressure lifts the PO check on A and pilots open the PO check on B; return flow from B routes through the spool to the T rail.

Actuation B (OPEN): Flow travels from P rail through compensator and spool to B port; pressure lifts the PO check on B and pilots open the PO check on A; return flow from A routes through the spool to the T rail.
Relief: Excessive pressure on A or B work port lines overcomes the respective port relief valve spring (set to 135), dumping fluid directly to the tank rail.
